beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You can't really share an agent.
beats.got: Sharing an agent is more complicated than buying seats, and there are four options.

beats.trigger: a tool people can open and mostly don't
beats.got: I know this one. We have a licence nobody uses.

beats.trigger: **Find** the absorption bottleneck and draft a technical plan and a people plan side by side
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: And why that one?
beats.got: The question is about preferences, not cost. I have no view on a Slack bot versus a skill.

beats.trigger: Your teammate doesn't want your agent. They want a job done.
beats.got: Start from the job to be done, not the tool. That is sensible.

beats.trigger: It should name one teammate, their current way of doing the job, and an outcome you could observe.
beats.got: The agent writes a one-page job description for one colleague, with an observable outcome. 'Observable' I can use.

beats.trigger: If the reason is *"we already have the platform,"* send it back.
beats.got: Don't choose by what's convenient for IT. I agree with that, though there is still no cost on any of the four.

beats.trigger: turns it into a technical plan plus a people plan
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can absorb it
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: Find the one root obstacle instead of a long risk list. That is how I read a risk register.

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: An empty owner column is a result in itself. It names a risk before I have to raise it. Still no budget line.

beats.trigger: checks the assumptions underneath these plans
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: The plans are guesses until tested.

beats.trigger: what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?
beats.got: Treat adoption as a falsifiable test. List two or three conditions and check them.

beats.trigger: Six months from now, the teammate went back to the incumbent. The agent writes three failure stories.
beats.got: A pre-mortem with three stories. The output is one person, one question, one test, which is concrete. I'd skip the stories.

beats.trigger: ## Lecture: Access is not absorption
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Accountability is the part with a name on it, and a name does not travel inside a folder.
beats.got: A shared agent is missing someone who answers for it. Abstract, and I'd rather see an example.

beats.trigger: Different challenges want different strategies, and different people absorb different ones.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The two get reported as one number and they are not one thing.
beats.got: Licences sold or seats activated measure access, not use. I report that number and it is the wrong one. I'd want a number for the other half.

beats.trigger: Then name what would have had to change in people's weeks for them to use it.
beats.got: Work out why the tool I paid for is not used. That is my own case, so I'd do it.

beats.trigger: The proposal got neither a yes nor a no.
beats.got: Even a good agent analysis stalled because leadership had not done the work themselves. I have seen this. No cost or payback was given, so it is an anecdote.

beats.trigger: Your candidate is not competing with nothing. It is competing with that.
beats.got: The competitor is the current way of working, such as a spreadsheet or a colleague. That is a fair baseline for any payback case.

beats.trigger: Send that person one message asking for twenty minutes on how they do the job now.
beats.got: The next step is one message to one person, with no new budget. I can do that.

beats.trigger: Compare your choice with a neighbour's, then run the debrief.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Access is a switch someone flips. Absorption happens in other people's weeks, at their pace, for their reasons.
beats.got: A recap of the lecture's point.

beats.trigger: One real conversation tells you more about absorption than a finished plan does.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: In Module 8 you ask what changes when you don't have to build each agent by hand.
beats.got: nothing new

take_homes: Seats activated is not use. The adoption number I get now measures access, not absorption, and I'd stop reporting it as one thing.
A new tool competes with whatever people do today (spreadsheet, colleague, gut call). Ask what would have to be true for them to switch.
An empty owner column in a rollout plan is a finding. I'd ask who answers for it.

monday.move: Ask my controller 20 minutes about how the month-end variance commentary gets done today, before showing any tool. Check the unused-licence number I currently report.
monday.stop_condition: If the controller says the current process works fine and no one can state an observable outcome, I drop it.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data, and there is still no cost per user.

misconception.why: The point that a licence gives access but not use hit my own unused-licence case. I still think of it mostly as spend. I now accept that someone has to own getting it used, but nothing here told me what that costs.

one_line: Decent on why bought tools sit unused and on the one-person next step, but it never gave me a number or a cost, and the first half was too abstract.
